newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps tick down, except late CFDs gains.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps tick down, except late CFDs gains.

text.p: European oil swaps were generally a touch easier on Tuesday except for Brent CFDs which kicked up towards the end of the day on the back of a physical deal.

Brent crude CFDs gained ground with balance of this week heard talked around -13/14 cents below July Brent compared with -20 cents on Monday, while next week was at -15 cents compared with -19 cents. Further out values were actually a touch easier with June 9-13 talked around -20 cents against July compared with -19 cents.
A June 30-July 4 CFD was traded at July -22 cents and June 16-20 was concluded at July -20 cents earlier in the day.

Heavy fuel swaps slipped by $1-1.50 a tonne primarily on the back of weaker physical trades but low sulphur fuel resisted any pull down and actually firmed. Traders said June traded at $98, about $1 a tonne higher than Monday talk.

Heavy fuel June traded at $84.00 and $84.50 having touched as low as $83.50 although nothing traded at this level. A 3Q barge traded at $87.75 and a 3Q cargo was concluded at $88.25 cif. A 4Q was done at $94, about 50 cents easier.

Gas oil swaps saw heavy diesel action with June EN590 trading at $10 over at least twice with $9.50 also done twice. Dealers said 0.2 pct was traded at -$9.75 under the June screen basis Med while 3Q was done at -$9.75 under 3Q.
Jet swaps also experienced a touch more business with June done at $20 and Q3 done at $24.

Gasoline swaps came under pressure with June talked at $207, July $5-5.50 below and August about $2 further out. Prompt physical barges changed hands at $207 and $207.25 fob ARA with $206.25 done on Antwerp.
Naphtha was broadly steady with June hovering around $191.
